courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

lectures.title: How Styling & Theming Works in Ionic Apps

cues.en: When we dive into styling and theming Ionic apps,
we've got a couple of concepts that all are kind of working together.
We've got a theme,
we got CSS variables which will play an important role,
we got the grid we already had a look at which also is kind of related to how our components look and
feel, we've got attributes like the color attribute on buttons that allow us to style components,
we got custom CSS styles we could write or custom Sass styles, doesn't matter,
so how do all these things work together,
what's up with all these different ways of adjusting the look of our application?
Well let's go through them step-by-step and you'll see that they actually all kind of work together.
The four important concepts
we can differentiate or we will have a look at are the general theme of the app, CSS variables,
then how we can work with components and their attributes and how we can actually also write our
own CSS or Sass rules to adjust the app to our requirements.
Now with theme, I mean a collection of general settings that influence the app-wide styling.
Now that means things like setting some base colors, some base sizes, base margins, so all these general
settings which will then be reflected across your entire app, across all your components and we'll actually
implement the theme through a concept called CSS variables,
so that is how these come into play.
Now CSS variables in case you're not aware of what that is,
CSS variables are a bit like Sass variables but if you don't know that, that's probably not helping
you either, right?
So CSS variables are in the end variables you can define in CSS where you can store values like
a color,
so a hex code for example or some margins or simply any units, you could store 20 pixels or 2rem
in a CSS variable and then you can assign that CSS variable as a value to your normal CSS
properties, so you could say the background color of this item should use the CSS variable
xyz and then you only need to declare that variable once and whenever you change that, all places
in your app that refer to it will automatically change and that is very powerful.
The difference to Sass variables is that CSS variables are baked into modern browsers and therefore
you don't need to compile them and you could then even change them at runtime which is not possible
with Sass variables.
So this is how CSS variables will come into play and of course, we'll have a look at how they work
and how we could create our own ones and how we use them and they are used in this theming process where
you use CSS variables to set up these base colors and so on.
Now you can always overwrite your theme at a component level though, so if you generally say I have a blue
main colour but for this specific button, you want to have a red background, that is always possible and
therefore, you should think of this theming process
as a general ruleset for your entire app to set up a general app identity, a general look and feel. Now
the CSS variables as I mentioned help us with that, in Ionic,
they can also be used to overwrite default components styles and I will show you how this works in this
module too.
You can use them as I mentioned to reuse CSS property values,
so to define a value once and then use it in multiple places of your app and you can even add your own
variables, Ionic gives you a lot of built-in ones which you can just overwrite but you can also of course
create your totally new ones which you then use in your own CSS code. So use CSS variables to set
dynamic reusable styles or values for styles. Now what about components like the Ionic grid or the different
attributes like color we can pass to different components?
Well in the end, these components and these attributes, like the color attribute of a button, they are adjustable
through CSS variables because they in the end just consume your general theme.
So the idea here is just that you can then use a declarative approach to set the color of a button in
a template but based on your general settings. So you could say this button should use my primary color
but what the primary color is is defined through your theme.
You could choose from a collection of default styles,
so for example a button accepts the color attribute where you can choose from nine different colors
Ionic understands and you can also of course combine that with custom styles.
So by default, the color property of a button refers to the global theme you set up but no one's stopping
you from writing your own CSS rule where you select a button by tag, by ID, by class, whatever you
want and you style it however you want,
you can set up any custom CSS code and that custom CSS code will then overwrite the globally
configured styles.
So we're using components and attributes to adjust styling per component and page,
we can color the button with the color attribute with the primary color on page one
and with the secondary color on page two
but we do configure it declaratively, so in the template. And now custom CSS code may use
your CSS variables, you can tap into those in your custom CSS code as well,
no one's stopping you from that
and you write custom CSS to style anything, you can style your Ionic app just the way you want
because it is a normal web app in the end and therefore, you can style every element, be that an Ionic element
or a normal HTML element in whichever way you want.
You can use custom CSS rules to overwrite other base styles,
so you could say this button normally would have the primary color but I will color it red
and no one's stopping you from doing that
and of course you can also add missing styles.
So if you're saying this item here should have a width of 300 pixels and you can't really achieve
this with the Ionic grid and so on,
well then you can just select that item and write your own CSS rule to make it 300 pixels wide and
you're done,
so you use your custom CSS styles for finetuning.
This is how these things all work together and this is
now what we'll go through over the next lectures in this module.
